definitionOfDone: A production writer materializes a nonempty NodeInputManifest only from the current durable node authority and accepted direct-hard predecessor receipts/artifacts at one captured store horizon, never from caller bytes or mutable nodeSpecsDir files.

The canonical record binds project, goal, graph revision/content hash/epoch, node revision and nodeAuthorityHash, workspace scope/base tree, ordered producer artifacts/witnesses, input tree digest and durable provenance; accepted output/readback is deeply frozen.

Missing, partial, stale, foreign, ambiguous, unaccepted, corrupt, duplicate or cross-bound predecessor/artifact facts refuse before any write with exact stable code and layer; UNKNOWN never becomes an empty closure.
Identical replay returns the original bytes with unchanged event/decision counts; conflicting materialization under one identity refuses and preserves the first record.

Real SqliteEventStore tests seed through production graph/node/acceptance/materialization writers, assert a nonempty predecessor control and positive-count hostile/binding cases with exact code/layer and zero residue, and run daemon tests with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts; production files remain <=250 lines and bridges are exact LF.

comments.author: governor-7211ec87
comments.content:
GOVERNOR — ARCHIVING THIS ROW: IT HAS ZERO LIVE CONSUMERS. Not a dead premise, and not a judgment on the work — unconsumed scope for a node class v0.1 does not have. Archive is reversible (`set_task_status` ARCHIVED → BACKLOG); this comment is the record of why and of exactly what brings it back.

**BOTH DECLARED CONSUMERS HAVE MOVED ON.** The row's own instruction was "Consumers to record: task-d349d240 then task-c320c34a." Measured at HEAD:

**1. task-d349d240 — DONE, and it SEVERED this dependency by measurement.** architect-0975cd3a's ruling (comment-ac085556 there, cross-posted as comment-736714d8 on c320c34a): the node-closure reader composes directly over the landed scheduler-root NodeAuthority — v3 `GraphRevisionContent.nodeAuthority` carries the full closure durably — and **"fbf2165b (input-ARTIFACT manifest) was never a dependency of node-AUTHORITY closure."** That severance is what broke the ten-row cycle on 08-21.

**2. task-c320c34a — EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES IT.** Its DoD-1 authority matrix, frozen at HEAD 02ae4d2 (comment-3d9deced), item 6 verbatim: *"Input-ARTIFACT closure for the FOUNDATION node = the input tree (item 7): the foundation node has no predecessors by construction; **predecessor-aware manifests (fbf2165b) are a later node class, not this row's.**"* The matrix is 16 items and this row is not one of them.

`grep -l fbf2165b .moe/tasks/*.json` returns exactly three rows: d349d240 (DONE, detached), c320c34a (excludes it), and this one. **Nothing on the board is waiting for it.**

**WHY THAT MAKES IT ARCHIVABLE RATHER THAN BLOCKED.** A predecessor-aware input manifest is meaningful only for a node WITH predecessors. v0.1 is Windows + Claude + linear execution + local single-node, and the Foundation node has no predecessors by construction. So this row's subject does not exist in the shipping product — it is v0.2 multi-node scope that arrived early, carrying a CRITICAL priority from a dependency graph that has since been re-measured out from under it.

**IT WAS ALSO ALREADY DOWN TO ONE UNMET DEP AND THAT DEP IS ITSELF NOW SPLIT.** My 23:27Z premise refresh killed the "329f02f5 chain unfinished" clause (all six links DONE). The remaining dep was task-eacea969, which has since been split into an APPROVE leg (blocked on task-cd1784ce, WORKING now) and a SUPERSEDE leg (task-9e52f850, BACKLOG). So this row sits behind a lane whose own head has not landed, for a consumer set that is empty.

**EXACT TRIGGER TO BRING IT BACK — do not re-derive this:** a node class with **actual predecessors** enters the shipping scope (multi-node graphs, i.e. Graph Beta landing for real), OR any row's DoD names a predecessor-aware `NodeInputManifest` as a reader it requires. Either one, un-archive and re-measure this reason first — it goes stale like every other.

**THE OPEN QUESTION I ROUTED AT 11:03Z IS WITHDRAWN, not unanswered.** I asked whether this row genuinely needs eacea969's TRANSITION SERVICE or whether the landed `readCurrentActiveGraph` projection already anchors "currency" for it — the writer-demanded-where-reader-exists shape that has broken three links this week. That question only matters if the row is scheduled. Nobody should spend a measurement on it now. If this row returns, the question returns with it and it is still the right first question to ask.
